original_question: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is W_{2k+2}-free, where W_{2k+2} is the even wheel on 2k+2 vertices, must lambda(G) be at most sqrt(4m/3), with equality only for regular complete 3-partite graphs?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 4.5 in Section 4 of arXiv:2512.19395 (the even-wheel edge-spectral Turán conjecture), rather than the broader general color-critical statement; the paper later notes that this conjecture is resolved by Theorem 4.7.
correct_elements: Your draft already has the correct forbidden graph family (the even wheel W_{2k+2}), the correct asymptotic regime (fixed k ≥ 2 and m large), the correct bound λ(G) ≤ √(4m/3), and the correct extremal family (regular complete 3-partite graphs). It is also aimed at the same narrow statement as the paper’s even-wheel conjecture, not a broader neighboring problem.
missing_details: The paper’s parameter m is the number of edges of G; your draft does not explicitly state that G has exactly m edges.
In the paper’s standard notation, G belongs to 𝒢(m, W_{2k+2}), which means not only W_{2k+2}-free but also having no isolated vertices.
The ambient class is finite, simple, undirected graphs.
λ(G) is the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix A(G).
The wheel notation is W_t = K_1 ∨ C_{t-1}; thus W_{2k+2} = K_1 ∨ C_{2k+1}, and ‘even wheel’ refers to the parity of its order.
‘m sufficiently large’ should be made explicit as: there exists m_0 = m_0(k) such that the statement holds for all m ≥ m_0.
For equality, ‘regular complete 3-partite graph’ means a balanced complete tripartite graph; hence equality can occur only for admissible edge counts m = 3t^2.
refined_question: For each fixed integer k ≥ 2, does there exist m_0 = m_0(k) such that every finite simple undirected W_{2k+2}-free graph G with m ≥ m_0 edges and no isolated vertices satisfies λ(G) ≤ √(4m/3), where λ(G) denotes the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix of G and W_{2k+2} = K_1 ∨ C_{2k+1}? Moreover, does equality hold if and only if G is a regular complete 3-partite graph (equivalently, a balanced complete tripartite graph)?
justification: The nearest official formulation matching your draft is Conjecture 4.5: it is the paper’s dedicated even-wheel statement and agrees with your draft in forbidden subgraph, asymptotic regime, numerical bound, and equality case. Section 1 supplies the hidden conventions needed to make it stand alone: graphs are finite, simple, and undirected; λ(G) is the adjacency spectral radius; and 𝒢(m, F) means F-free graphs with m edges and no isolated vertices. Section 3 gives the wheel notation W_t = K_1 ∨ C_{t-1}, so your interpretation of W_{2k+2} as the even wheel on 2k+2 vertices is correct. Although Theorem 4.7 later proves the conjecture as a special case of the general color-critical theorem, your draft is trying to capture the narrower conjectural formulation itself.
